questions.stem: The amendment procedure of the Indian Constitution is laid down in:
questions.explanation: Article 368 prescribes three modes of amendment: simple majority (for a few provisions), special majority of Parliament, and special majority + ratification by half the state legislatures (for federal-structure provisions). The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) held that Parliament cannot amend the 'basic structure'.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The words 'SOCIALIST', 'SECULAR' and 'INTEGRITY' were added to the Preamble by the:
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment (the 'mini-Constitution' during the Emergency, 1976) expanded the Preamble, added Fundamental Duties (Art 51A), widened DPSP, curbed judicial review. Many of its excesses were rolled back by the 44th Amendment (1978).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to:
questions.explanation: 73rd Amendment — Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) + 11th Schedule (29 subjects). Set up three-tier Panchayati Raj (Gram / Block / Zilla), mandatory elections every 5 years, reservation for SC/ST/women (33%). 74th Amendment (also 1992) did the same for urban bodies — Part IX-A + 12th Schedule.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 86th Amendment (2002) made RIGHT TO EDUCATION a Fundamental Right under Article:
questions.explanation: Article 21A — free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14. The RTE Act, 2009 operationalised this. Fundamental Duty 51A(k) was added simultaneously: parents must provide opportunities for education of their children between 6-14.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the 101ST CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT. 1. It introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) from 1 July 2017. 2. It inserted Article 279A creating the GST Council. 3. It added a new Article 246A giving concurrent powers to the Union and States to levy GST. 4. It abolished all state sales-tax entries from the Constitution. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 4 is WRONG — alcohol for human consumption and five petroleum products remain outside GST (still under state VAT/excise). 1, 2, 3 correctly describe the 101st Amendment, which enabled the dual GST (CGST + SGST + IGST) structure.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 103rd Amendment (2019) provides 10% reservation in government jobs and educational institutions to:

options.option_text: Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) of the general category

questions.explanation: 103rd Amendment — inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6). Provides 10% reservation for EWS among the 'general' (non-SC/ST/OBC) category. Upheld by the Supreme Court in Janhit Abhiyan (2022). Definition of EWS is by executive notification (annual family income threshold).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following CANNOT be amended merely by a SPECIAL majority of Parliament — i.e., requires ratification by half the state legislatures also?

options.option_text: Distribution of legislative powers between Centre and States (7th Schedule)

questions.explanation: Federal-structure provisions need state ratification: 7th Schedule (Union/State/Concurrent Lists), election of President, extent of executive power of Union/States, Supreme Court and High Courts, representation of states in Parliament, and Article 368 itself. The other items need only a special majority of Parliament.
